display.purpose: Panel/section headers, 600 weight, no separate display face.

body.purpose: Default reading size for prose, chat messages, field text.

label.purpose: Button text, tab labels, status badges, form labels.

mono.purpose: Raw LaTeX source view and compile error/log output.

shadows.name: ambient-card
shadows.purpose: The one base-level surface needing to visually detach from the page (ChatAssistant panel).

shadows.name: menu-lift
shadows.purpose: Dropdown menus and first-level menubar submenus at rest, always paired with ring-1 ring-foreground/10.

shadows.name: menu-lift-elevated
shadows.purpose: Nested/secondary menu levels sitting above a first-level menu.

motion.name: press-translate
motion.purpose: Active-state press feedback on tokenized buttons (active:translate-y-px).

motion.name: menu-slide-in
motion.purpose: Dropdown/menubar entrance direction keyed to anchor side.

components.name: Primary Button (tokenized)
components.description: Default shadcn Button primitive variant; near-black/near-white chrome action.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; gap: 0.375rem; height: 2rem; padding: 0 0.625rem; border-radius: 0.625rem; border: 1px solid transparent; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; background: oklch(0.205 0 0); color: oklch(0.985 0 0); transition: all 0.15s ease; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: color-mix(in oklch, oklch(0.205 0 0), transparent 20%); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: oklch(0.708 0 0); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px oklch(0.708 0 0 / 0.5); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(1px); }

components.name: Primary CTA (Compile Blue, as shipped)
components.description: Hardcoded primary action button as it actually appears on real screens (generate, save & compile, send).
components.css: .ds-btn-cta { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; justify-content: center; height: auto; padding: 0.5rem 1rem; border-radius: 0.25rem; border: none; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; background: #2563eb; color: #ffffff; } .ds-btn-cta:hover { background: #1d4ed8; } .ds-btn-cta:disabled { opacity: 0.5; pointer-events: none; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Tokenized text input primitive with focus ring and invalid state.
components.css: .ds-input { height: 2rem; width: 100%; min-width: 0; border-radius: 0.625rem; border: 1px solid oklch(0.922 0 0); background: transparent; padding: 0.25rem 0.625rem; font-size: 0.875rem; color: oklch(0.145 0 0); transition: border-color 0.15s, box-shadow 0.15s; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: oklch(0.556 0 0); } .ds-input:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: oklch(0.708 0 0); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px oklch(0.708 0 0 / 0.5); } .ds-input[aria-invalid='true'] { border-color: #dc2626; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgb(220 38 38 / 0.2); }

components.name: Active/Inactive Tab
components.description: PDF/Source result toggle and file tabs; binary active state using Compile Blue.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: flex; gap: 0.25rem; } .ds-tab { border-radius: 0.25rem; padding: 0.25rem 0.75rem; font-size: 0.875rem; background: #e4e4e7; color: #18181b; border: none; } .ds-tab-active { background: #2563eb; color: #ffffff; } .ds-tab:disabled { opacity: 0.4; }

components.name: Card (Chat Panel)
components.description: The one base-level surface carrying a shadow (ChatAssistant outer container).
components.css: .ds-card { border-radius: 0.875rem; border: 1px solid oklch(0.922 0 0); background: oklch(1 0 0); color: oklch(0.145 0 0); padding: 0.75rem; box-shadow: 0 1px 2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.05); }

components.name: Dropdown Menu
components.description: Overlay menu with the Ring-Over-Shadow elevation pattern.
components.css: .ds-menu { border-radius: 0.625rem; background: oklch(1 0 0); color: oklch(0.145 0 0); padding: 0.25rem; min-width: 8rem; box-shadow: 0 4px 6px -1px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1), 0 2px 4px -2px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); outline: 1px solid rgb(0 0 0 / 0.1); outline-offset: -1px; } .ds-menu-item { display: block; width: 100%; text-align: left; padding: 0.375rem 0.5rem; border-radius: 0.375rem; font-size: 0.875rem; background: transparent; border: none; } .ds-menu-item:hover { background: oklch(0.97 0 0); }

components.name: Chat Bubble (tinted)
components.description: Signature component: derives its tint live from --primary via relative OKLCH, the one part of the system built to survive an accent-color change without edits.
components.css: .ds-bubble { display: flex; max-width: 80%; width: fit-content; } .ds-bubble-content { border-radius: 0.875rem; padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem; font-size: 0.875rem; line-height: 1.625; background: oklch(from #2563eb 0.93 calc(c*0.4) h); color: oklch(0.145 0 0); word-break: break-word; }

narrative.overview: This is a tool, not a showroom, and it looks like one on purpose: a quiet, grayscale interface (stock shadcn/ui primitives on OKLCH neutrals) that gets out of the way of the actual product truth — a document either compiled or it didn't, and the interface's only job is to make that status legible fast. Nothing here is trying to be beautiful; it is trying to be trustworthy under repeated, high-stakes use (a student rerunning a thesis chapter compile for the fifth time at 2am). The one spot of color that exists — a Tailwind-stock blue (#2563eb) — has organically become the de facto accent across the real screens (active tabs, links, primary CTAs, in-progress status text), even though the underlying token system (--primary) is neutral grayscale and never actually references it. This is documented honestly below as the current, real state: a tokenized primitive layer (components/ui/*) that the application screens mostly bypass in favor of hardcoded Tailwind utility colors (blue-600, red-600, green-600, zinc-*). Named Compile Blue, this accent marks "the system is actively doing compile work or wants your attention here" — selection, action, progress — while red and green stay reserved for terminal states (error / success) surfaced from the actual Tectonic compile pipeline, never decorative. There is no invented visual sophistication here beyond what's implemented. Where the system is under-decided (no accent token wired into globals.css, screens hand-rolling their own blue), this file states that as the honest baseline and gives it a name, rather than smoothing it over into a token spec that doesn't exist in the code.
keyCharacteristics: Grayscale-first: identity lives in restraint, not palette.
One working accent (Compile Blue) doing double duty as brand color and status color — not yet formalized as a design token.
Status is truth: red/green/blue map directly to real compile-pipeline states, never used decoratively.
Density over drama: compact controls (h-7–h-9 buttons, text-sm/text-xs labels), tight padding, built for a working session, not a landing page.
Tonal at rest, shadow on overlay: cards and inputs are flat; dropdowns/menus/popovers lift with shadow-md/shadow-lg + a 1px foreground-tinted ring.

rules.name: The Compile Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue means "this is active, or this is the thing to press." It is never used for a resting/idle state and never used decoratively. If a new primary action or in-progress indicator is needed, it uses Compile Blue — do not introduce a second accent hue.

rules.name: The Status-Is-Truth Rule
rules.body: Red and green only ever reflect a real result from the actual compile/validation pipeline. Never use them for arbitrary UI emphasis unrelated to compile/save/delete outcomes.

rules.name: The One-Face Rule
rules.body: There is no separate display typeface. Hierarchy is built from weight and size within Geist Sans, not from font-pairing. Do not introduce a second UI typeface.

rules.name: The Ring-Over-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every overlay shadow ships with a ring-1 ring-foreground/10. The ring, not the shadow, is what actually reads in dark mode — never ship a popover shadow without it.

dos: Do use Compile Blue (#2563eb) for any new primary action or "in progress" indicator — it is already the de facto accent everywhere in the app; don't introduce a second accent hue.
Do reserve red/green strictly for real compile/save/delete outcomes (The Status-Is-Truth Rule).
Do default new overlay/popover components to shadow-md + ring-1 ring-foreground/10 (The Ring-Over-Shadow Rule) rather than shadow alone.
Do keep density high (compact h-7–h-9 controls, tight padding) — this is a working tool used in long sessions, not a marketing page that benefits from generous whitespace.

Do route new UI through the tokenized components/ui/* primitives (Button, Input, Bubble) rather than hand-rolling new Tailwind utility styling, to close the gap between the token layer and what screens actually render.
donts: Don't introduce a second brand/accent color. Compile Blue already carries that role; a second hue would fragment the "blue = active/action" signal.
Don't add shadows to base-level cards/inputs by default — the system is tonal-flat at rest; shadows are reserved for overlays and the one existing chat-panel exception.
Don't use red/green decoratively (e.g., a "fun" green success confetti unrelated to an actual compile result, or red used for anything other than an error/destructive action).
Don't ship a new primary CTA button without a visible focus-visible ring — the hardcoded blue CTAs currently lack one; this is a known gap to fix forward, not a pattern to repeat.
Don't add a second display typeface. Geist Sans/Geist Mono is the complete type system (The One-Face Rule).
